subject: rain gutter
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Gutters?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your gutters? The roof isn't what gets hurt.
One inch of rain on a thousand square feet of roof is about 600 gallons of water.
Within a season, leaves block the downspouts and every storm spills over the edge.
That water lands right beside your foundation, and starts seeping through cracks and joints into the basement.
After a few years, the soaked fascia boards rot, and winter ice dams push meltwater under the shingles.
Eventually the whole gutter can pull away and collapse. Twice a year with a ladder is the cheap option.

description:
What if you never cleaned your gutters? An inch of rain on 1,000 square feet of roof is roughly 600 gallons, and blocked gutters dump it beside the foundation, where it can seep into the basement.
Over time the fascia rots, ice dams form and the gutter itself can collapse. Delaware's environment agency and home experts suggest cleaning about twice a year.
